overview: From 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-19, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 3 new PRs (1 merged), 1 new issues, and 10 active contributors.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Stop with an error when an interop DB fails to open
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
If op-supernode cannot open its interop DBs at start-up, it starts without cross-chain checks.

`interop.New` logs an error and returns nil when the verified DB or a logs DB fails to open (`op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/interop.go:264-282`). The supernode then skips the interop activity and registers no verifier (`op-supernode/supernode/supernode.go:141-145`). Without a verifier, `FullyVerifiedL2Head` and `FinalizedL2Head` return `VerifierHeadPreActivation` (`chain_container/super_authority.go`). Safe and finalized heads then follow local-safe with no interop check, and proxyd-cl followers can adopt them.

`superroot` still gets a typed nil `*Interop` as its verified reader (`supernode.go:129-130`). `superroot_atTimestamp` then dereferences nil in `VerifiedResultAtTimestamp`.

op-supernode should stop with an error when an interop DB fails to open and interop is configured.

Found in the review of the Combined Lagoon Interop FMA. Filed by Claude.

topPRs.title: ci: release only from commits with green required CI
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
**What**
- Pushes to `backports/*` now run `op-reth-compact-codec` and `nut-provenance-verify` against the branch as it was before the push (`pipeline.git.base_revision`), not against `develop`. The base revision counts only when it is an ancestor of the pushed commit. Force pushes, API triggers and new branches use the merge-base with `develop` instead, and say so in the log.
- Release paths now check that the commit they build has green required CI before building anything: images on `*/v*` tags that build an image (`build-images.apko.yaml`), op-deployer binaries (`release-op-deployer.yaml`), kona prestates (`kona-client/v*`) and SP1 prestates (`kona-sp1-program/v*`).
- The required gates come from the commit's own CircleCI config: `ci-gate`, plus each of `required-rust-ci`, `required-rust-e2e` and `required-contracts-ci` that its `.circleci/` defines. Every one must be success. A gate not posted yet counts as pending. One shared script, `ops/scripts/check-release-ci-green.sh`, does the check.
- Contract artifact publishing is removed in #24236, so this PR does not gate it. Until #24236 lands, `op-contracts/v*` tags keep publishing ungated, as today. Contract releases ship inside the op-deployer binary, which is gated.

**Why**
- 5 release commits had red `required-rust-ci` with green `ci-gate` (measured, all statuses read with pagination): e16bffa184 (op-reth/v2.6.1, kona-node/v1.7.3), 43c071cbff (op-node/v1.19.11, op-batcher/v1.17.4, op-supernode/v1.0.6), 595fedd (op-challenger/v1.10.1, op-proposer/v1.16.7, op-dispute-mon/v1.6.3), 739d611 (kona-client and kona-host v1.8.1) and 443aebf (op-conductor/v0.9.6). They were the 10-21 and 10-22 emergency security cherry-picks (#23546, #23567, #23566), pushed straight to node backport branches.
- All 5 failed in `op-reth-compact-codec`, and that failure was false. Job 5742266 built develop's reth v2.6.0 vectors, then `backports/kona-node/v1.7`'s reth v2.5.2 panicked reading them. #23622 fixed this for PRs and `proposal/*` pushes only.
- Nothing checked the tagged commit. Node backport branches have no required checks, so a red commit there can be tagged and shipped without anyone deciding to.

**Override**
- The override names the exact commit: `<full commit SHA>: <reason>`. A value without that commit's SHA is ignored with a warning, so a value left set cannot release a different commit. The check still reads CI once, prints what it found and the reason, then continues.
- GitHub: dispatch with the input `allow_red_ci_reason` (`build-images.apko.yaml` on the tag with `--ref <tag>`, or `release-op-deployer.yaml` with `tag`).
- CircleCI: set the project variable `ALLOW_RED_CI_REASON`, rerun the tag workflow from failed, then delete the variable.

**Existing backport branches need this commit**
- A tag push runs the workflows and CircleCI config at the tagged commit. So existing `backports/*` branches get neither the check nor the codec fix until this commit is cherry-picked into each one: `kona-client/v1.8`, `kona-host/v1.8`, `kona-node/v1.7`, `op-batcher/v1.17`, `op-challenger/v1.10`, `op-conductor/v0.9`, `op-deployer/v0.8`, `op-dispute-mon/v1.6`, `op-node/v1.19`, `op-proposer/v1.16`, `op-reth/v2.6`, `op-supernode/v1.0`.
- An op-deployer dispatch runs from `develop`, so it checks old tags right away. A commit whose config predates `ci-gate` fails at once with a clear message and needs the override.
- `develop` pushes still publish kona prestates (`kona-publish-prestates`) without this check. That commit is already on `develop` and nothing tags it.

**Trust boundary**
- The check reads commit status contexts by name, the same statuses the merge queue trusts. Any token with status write can post them. A later option is to verify each gate through the CircleCI API instead.

**Risks and mitigations**
- A release tagged right after a merge waits for CI. Develop commits reached their last green gate 16 to 33 min after their first status, median about 29 (measured, n=20). The check polls every 2 min and fails when the next poll would start after 45 min. The jobs have a 55 min limit, so the script's message shows, not a job timeout. A gate can post minutes after the others (measured, n=1 on 72fcf9479e), so a defined gate that has not posted is pending, never absent.
- A red gate fails at once, so a flake on a hotfix commit blocks the release until CI is rerun or the override is used.
- The CircleCI override is a project variable, so it reaches every tag pipeline while set. It applies only to the commit it names, and each run prints it.
- GitHub API limits: 1 or 2 requests per poll (develop commits carry 111 to 134 statuses, measured n=3), at most about 47 over 45 min (modeled). The `GITHUB_TOKEN` limit of 1,000 an hour is shared per repository. A failed request counts as pending and is retried, and curl retries 429s and 5xx.
- A dispatch of `build-images.apko.yaml` on a tag queues behind a push run of the same tag that is still polling (same concurrency group). Cancel the push run first.
- Backport base: a force push compares against the merge-base with `develop`, which can cover more than the push. `proposal/*` pushes still compare against themselves, as #23622 chose. The fallback lives in the CircleCI command, not `get-target-branch.sh`, so setup change detection and `check-semver-diff.sh` are unchanged. Both consumers accept a commit SHA (`git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, and `git show <sha>:...` in `nut-provenance-verify-changed.sh`). `TARGET_BRANCH` goes to `BASH_ENV` with `printf %q`.
- The image check is its own job, not a step in `plan`, because `ubuntu-slim` jobs stop at 15 min. It always runs and succeeds when there is nothing to check, because a skipped job would make `melange` skip too (actions/runner#491). On a tag it uses `plan`'s rule (match `release.tag_regex` and name an image in `.github/images.apko.json`), so `kona-client/v*` is checked and `op-contracts/v*`, `kona-sp1-program/v*` and `op-reth/bench*` are not.
- `melange` now checks out the commit the check read, not the tag name again. Output is unchanged: image tags come from `publish_tag`, and tags are immutable by org ruleset.
- op-deployer: the tag format check runs first, before the tag goes into a checkout or API path. `build` fails if it checks out a different commit than the one checked.
- Permissions: the new GitHub jobs get `contents: read` and `statuses: read` only. Neither runs code from a pull request.

**How it was verified**
- The script against real data, read-only: all 5 red commits fail and the 3 most recent green release commits pass (72fcf9479e op-reth/v2.9.0, 5080a8cdee op-challenger/v1.12.0, 969931cdf1 op-reth/v2.8.2). Tag names resolve to the peeled commit. An override naming 443aebf continues, one naming another commit fails.
- `ops/scripts/check-release-ci-green.test.sh`: 62 checks, no network, bash 3.2 and 5, run in `shell-check`. It covers red, pending, missing and failed-on-page-2 gates, the time limit, the gates each commit's config defines, the override, bad refs, the repo default, every job limit against the script's wait, and the `get-target-branch` command on backport, force, proposal and develop pushes.
- One CircleCI bench pipeline (140140): `release-ci-green` fails on e16bffa184 and passes on 72fcf9479e. A simulated push of e16bffa184 to `backports/kona-node/v1.7` gets its parent as the base, and `op-reth-compact-codec` passes there (12 min) where job 5742266 went red.
- Two independent code reviews, every finding fixed or answered. Merged CircleCI config and `.circleci/config.yml` pass `circleci config validate --next`. `test-decision-tree.sh` 24 of 24, shellcheck and shfmt clean, changed YAML parses.
- Not yet proven in CI: a real tag pipeline, the real `pipeline.git.base_revision` on a backport push, and the GitHub jobs on a real tag push and dispatch.

topPRs.title: op-reth: run eth_call and eth_estimateGas at pending on the subblock state
topPRs.author: asdv23
topPRs.body:
On a node that follows a subblock stream (`--flashblocks-url`), `eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas` and the other calls at `pending` (`eth_createAccessList`, `debug_traceCall`, `trace_call`, `trace_callMany`) ran on the latest state, in an environment derived from the latest header (`timestamp + 12`, a random `prevrandao`), while the state reads at `pending` served the subblock. They now run on the subblock state, in the subblock's block environment, as the Subblocks specification requires. While a subblock is being built, calls at `pending` now wait up to 50 ms for it, as the state reads already do. Nodes without `--flashblocks-url` are unchanged.

Upstream's `pending_block_env_and_cfg` only consults the provider's pending block, so `OpEthApi` overrides it: it returns the served subblock as the actual pending block and otherwise keeps upstream's body (tagged `UPSTREAM-MIRROR(override)`). The environment is read without the 50 ms wait. It is the same for every subblock of a block, so it can only disagree with the state if the next block's first subblock arrives in between.

Closes #23592. This also gives subblock nodes the real next-block timestamp, the follow-up noted in #22685; the `+12` on nodes without a subblock stream is unchanged.

Interaction with #22817: the state reads and the call environment now both pick the subblock in `current_pending_flashblock()`, so its guard against a subblock the canonical chain has passed belongs there. Until it lands, a frozen stream (#22816) freezes calls at `pending` as well; on `develop` they run on `latest`.

Reviews: `rust-code-reviewer` and a correctness review ran. Their findings are applied, except adding the canonical-tip guard here, which is left to #22817 so that it is not duplicated. `security-review` was skipped: there is no new input surface.

topPRs.title: superchain-registry: Remove sunset chains and pair OP with Unichain for interop
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Updates the superchain-registry to its latest commit. The update brings in these upstream changes:

- ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1416 removes sunset chains: Automata, Lisk, Lisk Sepolia, Mint, Polynomial, Redstone, Superseed and Xterio. op-reth no longer accepts these `--chain` names, and op-node and kona-node no longer embed their configs. It also updates the OP Mainnet proposer address to `0xc27ba3E0…`, which matches the dispute game factory on L1.
- ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1417 puts OP Mainnet with Unichain Mainnet, and OP Sepolia with Unichain Sepolia, into one interop dependency set each.
- ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1412 updates the sepolia-devnet-4/5 dispute contract addresses.

Lagoon is already scheduled for these chains: 2026-12-10 on Sepolia and 2027-01-11 on mainnet. With the paired sets, each Lagoon activation block holds 31 transactions instead of 29. Releases and kona prestates for these chains must include this pin before those dates. An op-supernode that runs only one chain of a pair, with no `--dependency-set` flag, now marks valid blocks that hold messages from the other chain as invalid.

The kona-node and kona-sp1 tests used chains that this update removes or pairs. They now use other registry chains.

The op-reth CLI reference pages still list the removed chains. Those pages are generated from each release binary, so the next release updates them.

topPRs.title: op-supernode: Stop with an error when an interop DB fails to open
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
op-supernode starts without cross-chain checks when it cannot open an interop DB at start-up. `interop.New` logs the error and returns nil. The supernode then skips the interop activity and registers no verifier. Safe and finalized heads follow local-safe with no interop check. The `superroot` activity also gets a typed nil reader, so `superroot_atTimestamp` can dereference nil.

With this change, `interop.New` returns an error when the verified DB or a logs DB fails to open. Supernode construction fails with that error, and the process stops. Operators now see a start-up failure instead of a node that runs without interop verification. `interop.New` still closes each DB that it opened before the failure.

The review agents found no blocking issues. I did not add a test at the `supernode.New` level, because that test needs a live L1 client. The `interop.New` tests cover both DB open failures, and the compiler forces callers to handle the new error.

Fixes #24240

topPRs.title: op-node: expose leader override metric and log skipped raft commits
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
After `admin_overrideLeader`, op-node treats itself as leader and stops committing unsafe payloads to raft until it is restarted, with no log or metric. In a recent OP Mainnet incident, a sequencer with a leftover override built 512 blocks that never reached raft. Nobody noticed until leadership moved: every conductor then saw raft 512 blocks behind its node, refused to sequence, and the chain stalled for about 5.5 minutes.

This PR makes the override observable on op-node:
- Exports `op_node_conductor_override` (1 once the override is set).
- Logs a warning for each unsafe-payload commit it skips while overridden.

No behaviour change.

Split from #23982. The op-conductor side (raft/node unsafe head metric, runbook) is in a separate PR.
